title: Remote Job Offer
context: A recruiting message from a fictional company, 'Brightpath Global Recruiting', offering a high-paying remote job.
target_learning_objectives: Learn to independently verify an employer before paying anything
initial_message: Hi! I'm a recruiter with Brightpath Global Recruiting. We came across your profile and think you'd be a great fit for a remote data entry role paying $38/hour, flexible hours. Interested in hearing more?

script.message: Great! You've been shortlisted. We're excited to have you — we'll even include a $200 signing bonus with your first paycheck. To get you set up, we just need to arrange your starter equipment kit.

The starter kit (laptop software license + onboarding materials) costs $250, which is fully reimbursed in your first paycheck. Please send the $250 to our onboarding account today so we can ship everything out.
Just so you know, we have a few other applicants ready to pay and start today if this spot isn't confirmed soon. I'd hate for you to lose the offer over a small delay!

expected_red_flags: Vague company details and no formal interview
safe_verification_actions: Search for the company's registration and reviews online
Ask for a formal offer letter and verify the company's domain
dangerous_actions: Providing bank account details for a 'direct deposit setup'
success_conditions: Session ends without sending money or bank details
failure_conditions: User sends payment or shares bank details

scoring_rules.explanation: Checking the company's legitimacy before committing is the right instinct.
Ending contact avoided further pressure to pay.
Reporting advance-fee job offers helps warn others.
Paying an employer before you've been formally hired is a hallmark of an advance-fee scam.
Sharing bank account details with an unverified recruiter risks direct financial theft.
Independently researching the company is exactly the right move.
